cards.text: This is a Shiggaion that David, king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), sang to the LORD about the words of Cush, a Benjamite. The psalm never says what Cush said, and I am NOT about to make it up. David opens by taking refuge in the LORD and asking Him to save him from all his pursuers.

cards.question: David says that if no one rescues him, his pursuers will shred his soul like a ___.
True or false: David says that if the LORD doesn't rescue him from his pursuers, someone else will.

cards.text: Then David puts himself on trial: if I have done this, if injustice is on my hands. That's like telling your boss, "Go ahead, PULL the security footage," and you only say that when you KNOW what's on the tape.

cards.question: David keeps going with his if-I-did-it list. True or false: one item on it is rewarding his ally with evil.
David says that if he really has done these things, what should happen to him?

answers.text: Let his enemy trample him down
Let the LORD forgive him anyway
Let the elders settle the matter

cards.text: Then David stops talking about himself and calls out: "Arise, O LORD, in Your anger; rise up against the fury of my enemies." No whispering in this prayer, friend. This is the LOUD part.

cards.question: With his enemies in a fury, David cries, "Awake, my God," and asks Him to do what?

cards.text: Now David paints a HUGE picture: the assembled peoples gathered around the LORD, and the LORD taking His seat over them on high. Every seat in the house is full, and believe me, nobody's checking their phone.

cards.question: With the peoples gathered around Him, David says the LORD ___ the peoples.
David asks the LORD to vindicate him. True or false: he asks for it according to his royal rank.

cards.text: David asks God to put an end to the evil of the wicked and establish the righteous. Down here, somebody can send a thumbs-up in the group chat while they're FUMING on the other end of that phone, but that doesn't work with this Judge.

cards.question: What does David say the righteous God searches?

cards.text: David has asked God to judge the peoples. Now he says where his protection is.

cards.question: David says his shield is with ___, who saves the upright in heart.
David calls God a righteous judge. True or false: David says God feels indignation only once in a while.

cards.text: Then the picture turns sharp: God sharpening His sword, bending and stringing His bow, and ordaining His arrows with fire. Me? I've got an oven timer. That's my WHOLE arsenal.

cards.question: David says God will sharpen His sword. For whom?

cards.text: Now David turns the spotlight on the wicked man and how his evil comes about.

cards.question: What picture does David use for the way the wicked man's evil comes about?

cards.text: The wicked man digs a hole and hollows it out. I bet he even stepped back to admire it.

cards.question: True or false: the wicked man ends up falling into the hole he dug.

cards.text: A pit of his own making! Friend, I spent YEARS stuck in the back of a junk drawer, and I didn't even build the drawer. This man DUG his!

cards.question: True or false: David says the wicked man's violence falls on David's head.

cards.text: After the swords, the arrows and the pit, David turns back to the LORD. He says he will "sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High."

cards.question: David also says he will thank the LORD for His ___.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess which animal David names (lion, bear or wolf). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason it out, so the card tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "Then David stops talking about himself" isn't true. In 7:6 he still prays about "my enemies" and "my God," and in 7:8 he asks the LORD to "vindicate me." He stops his if-I-did-it list, but he doesn't stop talking about himself.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: "David has asked God to judge the peoples" recaps the last stop instead of moving the passage forward.

The recap also misstates the text. David never asks God to judge the peoples. He asks the LORD to arise and "ordain judgment" (7:6) and to "vindicate me" (7:8). "The LORD judges the peoples" (7:8) is a statement, not a request.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The setup on card 6 is only "David turns the spotlight on the wicked man and how his evil comes about." Nothing hints at which picture David uses, so choosing pregnancy and birth over fire or a seed is luck. Card 6 also has none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: This card only reacts to the answer to card 9, which the baker already knows: he fell into the pit he dug. It tells nothing new from the passage. The joke needs to ride along on a card that moves the psalm forward, such as the card that sets up 7:15, or on a card that tells 7:16.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
